text:
maya: heads up — found a confusing goroutine leak in the go sample app when cancelling generator streams mid-handshake. repro attached.
kevin: ugh. can you paste the stack trace or snippet? is this the auth refresh + stream cancel case?
maya: yeah. steps: start generator, token refresh triggers during initial handshake, then ctx cancel. goroutines stuck in `stream.readLoop` with blocked recv on auth-ch updates. stack: `goroutine 42 [chan receive]: \n  github.com/redwood/inference/sdk-go/stream.(*conn).readLoop(0xc000...)
  /.../stream/conn.go:112 +0x...`
kevin: hmm. sounds like the client cancels but the auth refresh goroutine keeps trying to handshake. we have similar race in py/ts but their SDKs swallow and close underlying net.Conn earlier.
andre: parity concern — if we change semantics in go we need to keep behavior consistent across languages or document difference. Go users expect explicit `Close()` semantics.
sam: maybe the root is generator API ergonomics. two patterns: (A) iterator style where user calls `Next(ctx)` which respects ctx, or (B) callback/chan style where the runtime owns goroutines and returns a channel. we currently expose (B) and it leaks on mid-handshake cancels.
maya: my quick hack: make handshake cancellable by passing ctx down to auth refresh and accept a `handshakeCtx` we cancel on user ctx cancel. patch here: ```diff
- go:handshake := make(chan struct{})
+ go:handshakeCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
+ defer cancel()
+ // pass handshakeCtx into authRefresh
```
kevin: that helps but still worried about complexity. can we instead add a small API change: `Generator.Pull(ctx, opts) (Stream, error)` where Stream has a `Close()` and `Recv(ctx) (Chunk, error)`. That way ownership is explicit and `Recv` always respects ctx deadlines.
andre: `Recv(ctx)` matches other SDKs `client.receive` styles. it's ergonomic but a breaking change for current users. we could add it as V2 API while keeping current `Subscribe` for compat.
sam: tests: i wrote a tiny harness that simulates token refresh race. results: current impl leaks ~3 goroutines per cancel, `Recv(ctx)` impl shows zero leaks. link: https://ci.internal/redwood/streams/repro/3724
ci-bot: build 3724 failed on `TestGeneratorCancelRace` — reproducer included in PR #4621.
maya: ok will open a RFC PR for v2-stream API w/ `Recv(ctx)` and explicit Close. include migration guide + minimal shim from old API to new that returns a goroutine-managed stream but warns in logs.
kevin: add a test matrix: ensure python/ts parity or at least documented differences. also add a sample app updated in `sdk/go/examples/generator-cancel`.
andre: UX nit — make example show both `defer stream.Close()` and `for { chunk, err := stream.Recv(ctx); if err!=nil { break } }`. newbies copy that.
sam: ping me for benchmarks. I'll run latency/cpu perf to ensure per-request overhead not huge.
maya: thanks. i'll open RFC + PR with repro + new example. tagging @kevin @andre @sam for review :thumbsup:
kevin: cheers. please include a small changelog entry for console docs about generator behavior and a migration note for Dedicated customers.
